sentences.zh: 諸禁軍名額系捧日、天武、龍衛、神衛爲上軍，五百文已上料錢見錢爲中軍，不滿五百文料錢見錢並捧日天武第五第七軍、龍衛神衛第十軍、驍猛、雄勇、驍雄、雄威爲下軍。

translations.literal: Palace Corps titles and quotas: Sun-Holding, Heavenly Martial, Dragon Guard, and Divine Guard were upper armies; those with grain-pay cash of five hundred cash or more were middle armies; those with grain-pay cash below five hundred cash, together with Sun-Holding and Heavenly Martial Fifth and Seventh Armies, Dragon Guard and Divine Guard Tenth Armies, Fierce Bold, Bold Courage, Fierce Bold, and Bold Prestige, were lower armies.
translations.idiomatic: Among Palace Corps titles and quotas, Sun-Holding, Heavenly Martial, Dragon Guard, and Divine Guard ranked as upper armies; units paid five hundred cash or more in grain-pay cash counted as middle armies; units paid less than five hundred cash, together with Sun-Holding and Heavenly Martial Fifth and Seventh Armies, Dragon Guard and Divine Guard Tenth Armies, Fierce Bold, Bold Courage, Fierce Bold, and Bold Prestige, ranked as lower armies.

sentences.zh: 元豐五年十月，詔諸路教閱廂軍，於下禁軍內增入指揮名額，排連並同禁軍。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fifth year of Yuanfeng, an edict ordered that Comforter Corps under training review in the various routes should, within lower Palace Corps, add command titles and quotas, with company and platoon organization the same as Palace Corps.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Yuanfeng 5, an edict ordered training-review Comforter Corps in every route to take command titles and quotas from lower Palace Corps ranks, with company and platoon organization matching Palace Corps.

sentences.zh: 蓋熙寧之籍，天下禁軍凡五十六萬八千六百八十八人；

translations.literal: Under the Xining registry, Palace Corps throughout the realm totaled 568,688;
translations.idiomatic: Under the Xining registry, Palace Corps empire-wide totaled 568,688;

sentences.zh: 元豐之籍，六十一萬二千二百四十三人。

translations.literal: under the Yuanfeng registry, 612,243.
translations.idiomatic: under the Yuanfeng registry, 612,243.

sentences.zh: 紹聖四年，陝西路增置蕃落馬軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Shaosheng, the Shaanxi route added Tribal Frontier mounted troops.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaosheng 4, the Shaanxi route added Tribal Frontier mounted troops.

sentences.zh: 是年，蘭州金城置步軍保捷、馬軍蕃落。

translations.literal: That year, at Jincheng in Lanzhou, Foot Secure Swift and Mounted Tribal Frontier were established.
translations.idiomatic: That same year, at Jincheng in Lanzhou, Foot Secure Swift and Mounted Tribal Frontier were established.

sentences.zh: 元符元年，利州路興元府、閬州各增置就糧武寧；

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanfu, Xingyuan Prefecture and Lang Prefecture in Lizhou route each added Grain-Pay Martial Tranquility;
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanfu 1, Xingyuan Prefecture and Lang Prefecture in Lizhou route each added Grain-Pay Martial Tranquility;

sentences.zh: 又湖北、江東各增置有馬雄略。

translations.literal: Hubei and Jiangdong each also added Mounted Bold Strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Hubei and Jiangdong each also added Mounted Bold Strategy.

sentences.zh: 涇原路新築南牟會，賜名西安州，戍守共以七千人爲額，仍招置馬軍蕃落、步軍保捷。

translations.literal: On the Jingyuan route a new fort was built at Nanmouhui, granted the name Xi'an Prefecture; garrison strength was fixed at seven thousand, with recruitment of Mounted Tribal Frontier and Foot Secure Swift.
translations.idiomatic: On the Jingyuan route Nanmouhui was newly fortified and named Xi'an Prefecture; garrison strength was fixed at seven thousand, with Mounted Tribal Frontier and Foot Secure Swift recruited.

sentences.zh: 天都、臨羌砦戍守各以三千人爲額，仍各置馬軍蕃落、步軍保捷。

translations.literal: Garrisons at Tiandu and Linqiang stockades were each fixed at three thousand, with Mounted Tribal Frontier and Foot Secure Swift established at each.
translations.idiomatic: Garrisons at Tiandu and Linqiang stockades were each fixed at three thousand, with Mounted Tribal Frontier and Foot Secure Swift established at each.

sentences.zh: 永興軍等路創置蕃落；

translations.literal: Yongxing Army and other routes newly established Tribal Frontier;
translations.idiomatic: Yongxing Army and other routes newly established Tribal Frontier;

sentences.zh: 河北大名府等二十二州共創置馬軍廣威、步軍保捷，以河北大水，招刺流民故也。

translations.literal: twenty-two prefectures including Daming Prefecture in Hebei jointly newly established Mounted Broad Awesome and Foot Secure Swift, because of the great flood in Hebei and recruitment of displaced people.
translations.idiomatic: twenty-two prefectures including Daming Prefecture in Hebei jointly raised Mounted Broad Awesome and Foot Secure Swift, to recruit displaced people after the great Hebei flood.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，環慶增置敢勇二百人。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the second year, Huanqing added two hundred Bold Courage troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the second year, Huanqing added two hundred Bold Courage troops.

sentences.zh: 四月，環慶路都總管司言：「本路新展定邊城，比之橫山、興平等處城砦尤深，乞增置住營馬軍蕃落、步軍保捷。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, the Huanqing Route Overall Command said: "This route has newly expanded Dingbian city; compared with stockades such as Hengshan and Xingping its depth is especially great—we beg to add stationed Mounted Tribal Frontier and Foot Secure Swift.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, the Huanqing Route Overall Command reported: "This route has newly expanded Dingbian city; compared with stockades such as Hengshan and Xingping it is especially deep—we ask to add stationed Mounted Tribal Frontier and Foot Secure Swift.

sentences.zh: 」六月，環慶路都總管司言：「展築慶州白豹城，合增置住營馬步軍。

translations.literal: " In the sixth month, the Huanqing Route Overall Command said: "Expanding and building Baibao city in Qing Prefecture requires adding stationed mounted and foot troops.
translations.idiomatic: " In the sixth month, the Huanqing Route Overall Command reported: "Expanding Baibao city in Qing Prefecture requires adding stationed mounted and foot troops.

sentences.zh: 」又鄜延路都總管司言：「本路新築米脂等八堡砦，合增置土兵、馬步軍。

translations.literal: " The Fuyan Route Overall Command also said: "This route has newly built eight forts and stockades including Mizhi; mounted and foot troops and local militia should be added.
translations.idiomatic: " The Fuyan Route Overall Command also reported: "This route has newly built eight forts and stockades including Mizhi; local militia plus mounted and foot troops should be added.

sentences.zh: 」皆從之。

translations.literal: " All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: " All were approved.

sentences.zh: 三年，樞密院奏：「河北增置馬軍廣威、步軍保捷二萬餘人，欲令揀選升換在京闕額軍分。

translations.literal: In the third year, the Bureau of Military Affairs memorialized: "Hebei has added more than twenty thousand Mounted Broad Awesome and Foot Secure Swift; we wish to have them selected and transferred to fill vacant Palace Corps slots in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, the Bureau of Military Affairs memorialized: "Hebei has added more than twenty thousand Mounted Broad Awesome and Foot Secure Swift; we propose selecting them for transfer to fill vacant Palace Corps slots in the capital.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " Approval was given.
translations.idiomatic: " Approval was given.

sentences.zh: 自紹聖以來，陝西、河東連用兵六年，進築未已，覆軍殺將，供給不可勝紀。

translations.literal: Since Shaosheng, Shaanxi and Hedong had been at war continuously for six years; forward fortification did not cease; armies were destroyed and generals killed; supplies beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Since Shaosheng, Shaanxi and Hedong had fought continuously for six years; forward fortification never stopped; armies were wiped out and generals killed; supplies poured out beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 四年十一月，廣西路置刀牌手三千人，於切要州軍更戌，以寧海名。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fourth year, Guangxi route established three thousand blade-shield troops, rotating garrison at critical prefectures and armies, under the name Secure the Sea.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the fourth year, the Guangxi route raised three thousand blade-shield troops, rotating garrison at critical prefectures and armies, under the name Secure the Sea.

sentences.zh: 十二月，詔：「四輔屏翰京師，兵力不可偏重，可各以二萬人爲額。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, an edict: "The four auxiliary prefectures that screen the capital must not be over-heavy in troops; each may be fixed at twenty thousand as quota.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, an edict: "The four auxiliary prefectures that screen the capital must not be over-heavy in troops; each may be fixed at twenty thousand as quota.

sentences.zh: 」五年，環慶路進築徐丁台城，賜名安邊，置馬軍蕃落、步軍保捷。

translations.literal: " In the fifth year, the Huanqing route forward-built Xudingtai city, granted the name Secure the Border, and established Mounted Tribal Frontier and Foot Secure Swift.
translations.idiomatic: " In the fifth year, the Huanqing route forward-built Xudingtai city, named it Secure the Border, and established Mounted Tribal Frontier and Foot Secure Swift.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年，詔；

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingkang, an edict;
translations.idiomatic: In Jingkang 1, an edict:

sentences.zh: 「廣西宜、融二州實爲極邊，舊置馬軍難議減省，且依元降指揮招置。」

translations.literal: "Yi and Rong prefectures in Guangxi are truly on the outermost frontier; the mounted troops formerly established there are hard to reduce—we shall recruit according to the original edict."
translations.idiomatic: "Yi and Rong prefectures in Guangxi stand on the outermost frontier; the mounted troops formerly established there cannot easily be cut—we shall recruit according to the original edict."

sentences.zh: 自元豐而後，民兵日盛，募兵日衰，其募兵闕額，則收其廩給，以爲民兵教閱之費。

translations.literal: After Yuanfeng, local militia grew daily while recruited troops declined; vacancies in recruited troops had their grain pay collected and used for local militia training expenses.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuanfeng, local militia grew daily while recruited troops declined; when recruited quotas fell short, their grain pay was diverted to fund local militia training.

sentences.zh: 元祐以降，民兵亦衰。

translations.literal: From Yuanyou onward, local militia also declined.
translations.idiomatic: From Yuanyou onward, local militia declined as well.

sentences.zh: 崇甯、大觀以來，蔡京用事，兵弊日滋，至於受逃亡，收配隸，猶恐不足。

translations.literal: Since Chongning and Daguan, with Cai Jing in power, military abuses grew daily; even accepting deserters and enrolled convicts, they still feared the numbers were not enough.
translations.idiomatic: Since Chongning and Daguan, with Cai Jing in power, military abuses worsened by the day; even taking deserters and enrolled convicts, they still feared the ranks were not full enough.

sentences.zh: 政和之後，久廢蒐補，軍士死亡之余，老疾者徒費廩給，少健者又多冗占，階級既壞，紀律遂亡。

translations.literal: After Zhenghe, long-abandoned recruitment and replacement left, among dead soldiers, the old and sick wasting grain pay while the young and strong mostly held redundant posts; ranks collapsed and discipline perished.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhenghe, recruitment and replacement had long been neglected; among the dead and the living alike, the old and sick wasted grain pay while the young and strong mostly held phantom posts; ranks collapsed and discipline died.

sentences.zh: 童貫握兵，勢傾內外，凡遇陣敗，恥於人言，第申逃竄。

translations.literal: Tong Guan held military power, his influence overwhelming inside and outside; whenever a battle was lost, ashamed before others' words, he would report only flight and dispersal.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Guan held the army, his power overwhelming court and camp alike; whenever a battle was lost, too ashamed to admit defeat, he would report only flight and dispersal.

sentences.zh: 河北將兵，十無二三，往往多住招闕額，以其封樁爲上供之用。

translations.literal: Hebei commander troops were scarcely two or three in ten; many vacancies were deliberately left unfilled, their earmarked funds turned to tribute for the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Hebei commander troops were scarcely two or three in ten; many quotas were deliberately left vacant, their earmarked funds diverted as tribute to the capital.

sentences.zh: 陝右諸路兵亦無幾，種師道將兵入援，止得萬五千人。

translations.literal: Troops in the Shaanxi routes were also few; when Zhong Shidao led his army to reinforce the capital, he mustered only fifteen thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Troops in the Shaanxi routes were also few; when Zhong Shidao marched to reinforce the capital, he mustered only fifteen thousand.

sentences.zh: 故靖康之變，雖畫一之詔，哀痛激切，而事已無及矣。

translations.literal: Thus at the Jingkang crisis, though a uniform edict was issued, anguished and urgent, it was already too late.
translations.idiomatic: Thus when the Jingkang crisis came, though a uniform edict went out, anguished and urgent, it was already too late.

sentences.zh: 高宗南渡，始建御營司，未幾，復並御營歸樞密院。

translations.literal: After Gaozong crossed south, he first established the Imperial Camp Bureau; before long he again merged the Imperial Camp into the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozong crossed south, he first established the Imperial Camp Bureau; before long he merged the Imperial Camp back into the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 建炎四年，改御前五軍爲神武軍，御營五軍爲神武副軍，並隸樞密院。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianyan, the five Imperial Front armies were changed to Divine Martial Army, and the five Imperial Camp armies to Divine Martial Auxiliary Army, both subordinate to the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyan 4, the five Imperial Front armies became Divine Martial Army, and the five Imperial Camp armies Divine Martial Auxiliary Army, both under the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 五年，上以祖宗故事，兵皆隸三衙，乃廢神武中軍隸殿前司，於是殿司兵柄始一。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, the emperor, following ancestral precedent that all troops belonged to the three yamen, abolished the independent Divine Martial Central Army and subordinated it to the Palace Front Bureau; thus the Palace Front Bureau's military authority was unified at last.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, citing ancestral precedent that all troops belonged to the three yamen, the emperor abolished the independent Divine Martial Central Army and brought it under the Palace Front Bureau; at last the Palace Front Bureau held unified military authority.

sentences.zh: 乾道元年，詔殿前兵馬權以七萬三千人爲額。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qiandao, an edict provisionally fixed Palace Front horse and foot at seventy-three thousand as quota.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiandao 1, an edict provisionally fixed Palace Front horse and foot at seventy-three thousand.

sentences.zh: 諸屯駐大軍則皆諸將之部曲，高宗開元帥府，諸將兵悉隸焉。

translations.literal: The various garrisoned great armies were all the personal followings of individual generals; Gaozong opened a marshal headquarters and all generals' troops were subordinate to it.
translations.idiomatic: The various garrisoned great armies were all the personal followings of individual generals; Gaozong opened a marshal headquarters, and every general's troops fell under it.

sentences.zh: 建炎後，諸大將兵浸盛，因時制變，屯無常所。

translations.literal: After Jianyan, the great generals' armies gradually grew; adapting to the times, they had no fixed garrison.
translations.idiomatic: After Jianyan, the great generals' armies gradually swelled; adapting to the times, they had no fixed garrison.

sentences.zh: 如劉光世軍或在鎮江、池州、太平，韓世忠軍或屯江州、江陰，岳飛一軍或屯宜興、蔣山，王彥八字軍隨張浚入蜀，吳玠兵多屯鳳州、大散關、和尚原。

translations.literal: Liu Guangshi's army might be at Zhenjiang, Chizhou, or Taiping; Han Shizhong's at Jiangzhou or Jiangyin; Yue Fei's at Yixing or Jiangshan; Wang Yan's Eight-Character Army followed Zhang Jun into Shu; Wu Jie's troops mostly garrisoned Feng Prefecture, Dasanguan, and Heshang Plain.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Guangshi's army might be at Zhenjiang, Chizhou, or Taiping; Han Shizhong's at Jiangzhou or Jiangyin; Yue Fei's at Yixing or Jiangshan; Wang Yan's Eight-Character Army followed Zhang Jun into Shu; Wu Jie's troops mostly garrisoned Feng Prefecture, Dasanguan, and Heshang Plain.

sentences.zh: 是時合內外大軍十九萬四千餘，川、陝不與焉。

translations.literal: At that time, inner and outer great armies combined exceeded 194,000; Sichuan and Shaanxi were not included.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, inner and outer great armies combined exceeded 194,000; Sichuan and Shaanxi were not included.

sentences.zh: 及楊沂中將中軍總宿衛，江東劉光世、淮東韓世忠、湖北岳飛、湖南王𤫉四軍共十九萬一千六百，亦未嘗有屯。

translations.literal: When Yang Yizhong commanded the central army overseeing palace guard duty, Liu Guangshi in Jiangdong, Han Shizhong in Huai East, Yue Fei in Hubei, and Wang Yan in Hunan—the four armies totaled 191,600, and none had fixed garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Yizhong commanded the central army overseeing palace guard duty, Liu Guangshi in Jiangdong, Han Shizhong in Huai East, Yue Fei in Hubei, and Wang Yan in Hunan—the four armies totaled 191,600, and none had fixed garrisons.

sentences.zh: 紹興十一年，范同以諸將握兵難制，獻謀秦檜，且以柘皋之捷言於上，召張俊、韓世忠、岳飛入覲，張俊首納所部兵。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Shaoxing, Fan Tong, finding the generals' hold on troops hard to control, offered counsel to Qin Hui and also spoke to the emperor of the victory at Zhegao; Zhang Jun, Han Shizhong, and Yue Fei were summoned to audience, and Zhang Jun was first to surrender his troops.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 11, Fan Tong, finding the generals' hold on troops hard to control, advised Qin Hui and also told the emperor of the victory at Zhegao; Zhang Jun, Han Shizhong, and Yue Fei were summoned to court, and Zhang Jun was first to surrender his troops.

sentences.zh: 分命三大帥副校各統所部，自爲一軍，更銜曰統制御前軍馬。

translations.literal: The three great marshals' deputy commanders were each ordered to command their own followers as separate armies, with the new title Controller of Imperial Front Horse and Foot.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy commanders of the three great marshals were each ordered to lead their own followers as separate armies, bearing the new title Controller of Imperial Front Horse and Foot.

sentences.zh: 罷宣撫司，遇出師取旨，兵皆隸樞密院，屯駐仍舊。

translations.literal: The Pacification Commissions were abolished; when campaigns were launched orders were taken from court, and troops all belonged to the Bureau of Military Affairs, while garrisons remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: The Pacification Commissions were abolished; on campaign, orders came from court, all troops belonged to the Bureau of Military Affairs, and garrisons stayed as they were.

sentences.zh: 而四川大將兵曰興、成、階、鳳、文、龍、利、閬、金、洋、綿、房、西和州、大安軍、興元、隆慶、潼川府凡十七郡，亦分屯就糧焉。

translations.literal: Sichuan's great general armies garrisoned grain-pay in seventeen prefectures: Xing, Cheng, Jie, Feng, Wen, Long, Li, Lang, Jin, Yang, Mian, Fang, Xihe Prefecture, Da'an Army, Xingyuan, Longqing, and Tongchuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan's great general armies garrisoned grain-pay across seventeen prefectures: Xing, Cheng, Jie, Feng, Wen, Long, Li, Lang, Jin, Yang, Mian, Fang, Xihe Prefecture, Da'an Army, Xingyuan, Longqing, and Tongchuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 乾道之末，各州有都統司領兵：建康五萬，池州一萬二千，鎮江四萬七千，楚州武鋒軍一萬一千，鄂州四萬九千，荊南二萬，興元一萬七千，金州一萬一千。

translations.literal: At the end of Qiandao, overall command offices in each prefecture led troops: Jiankang 50,000, Chizhou 12,000, Zhenjiang 47,000, Chuzhou Martial Edge Army 11,000, E Prefecture 49,000, Jingnan 20,000, Xingyuan 17,000, Jin Prefecture 11,000.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Qiandao, overall command offices in each prefecture led troops: Jiankang 50,000, Chizhou 12,000, Zhenjiang 47,000, Chuzhou Martial Edge Army 11,000, E Prefecture 49,000, Jingnan 20,000, Xingyuan 17,000, Jin Prefecture 11,000.

sentences.zh: 其後分屯列戍，增損靡常。

translations.literal: Afterward, dispersed garrisons and frontier posts increased and decreased without fixed rule.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, dispersed garrisons and frontier posts waxed and waned without fixed rule.

sentences.zh: 所可考者，統制、統領、正將、副將、準備將之目也。

translations.literal: What can be verified are the titles Controller, Commanding General, Senior Commander, Deputy Commander, and Reserve Commander.
translations.idiomatic: What can be verified are the titles Controller, Commanding General, Senior Commander, Deputy Commander, and Reserve Commander.

sentences.zh: 至於水軍之制，則有加于前者，南渡以後，江、淮皆爲邊境故也。

translations.literal: As for the navy system, it exceeded what had gone before, because after the southern crossing the Yangtze and Huai became frontiers.
translations.idiomatic: The navy system exceeded what had gone before, for after the southern crossing the Yangtze and Huai had become frontiers.

sentences.zh: 建炎初，李綱請於沿江、淮、河帥府置水兵二軍，要郡別置水兵一軍，次要郡別置中軍，招善舟楫者充，立軍號曰淩波、樓船軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyan, Li Gang requested that along the Yangtze, Huai, and Yellow River command headquarters two naval armies be established, at key prefectures one naval army each, at secondary prefectures one central army each, recruiting skilled boatmen to fill them, with army names Wave-Cleaving and Tower-Ship Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianyan, Li Gang asked that along the Yangtze, Huai, and Yellow River command headquarters raise two naval armies, key prefectures one naval army each, secondary prefectures one central army each, recruiting skilled boatmen under the names Wave-Cleaving and Tower-Ship Army.

sentences.zh: 其戰艦則有海鰍、水哨馬、雙車、得勝、十棹、大飛、旗捷、防沙、平底、水飛馬之名。

translations.literal: Their warships bore the names Sea Porpoise, Water Scout Horse, Twin Cart, Victor, Ten Oars, Great Flyer, Banner Swift, Sand Guard, Flat Bottom, and Water Flying Horse.
translations.idiomatic: Their warships bore the names Sea Porpoise, Water Scout Horse, Twin Cart, Victor, Ten Oars, Great Flyer, Banner Swift, Sand Guard, Flat Bottom, and Water Flying Horse.

sentences.zh: 隆興以後至於寶祐、景定間，江、淮沿流堡隘相望，守禦益繁，民勞益甚。

translations.literal: From Longxing onward through Baoyou and Jingding, fortresses and passes lined the Yangtze and Huai currents; defense grew ever more elaborate and the people's labor ever heavier.
translations.idiomatic: From Longxing onward through Baoyou and Jingding, fortresses and passes lined the Yangtze and Huai currents; defense grew ever more elaborate and the people's burdens ever heavier.

sentences.zh: 迨鹹淳末，廣東籍蜑丁，閩海拘舶船民船，公私俱弊矣。

translations.literal: By the end of Xianchun, Guangdong registered Tanka boat people, and Minhai conscripted merchant and civilian vessels—the public and private sectors alike were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of Xianchun, Guangdong registered Tanka boat people and Minhai conscripted merchant and civilian vessels—public and private alike were ruined.

sentences.zh: 其禁軍將校，則有殿前司都指揮使、副都指揮使、都虞候各一人；

translations.literal: Palace Corps commanders included one Palace Front Bureau Overall Commander, one Deputy Overall Commander, and one Chief Adjutant each;
translations.idiomatic: Palace Corps commanders included one Palace Front Bureau Overall Commander, one Deputy Overall Commander, and one Chief Adjutant each;

sentences.zh: 諸班有都虞候、指揮使、都知、副都知、押班；

translations.literal: squads had Chief Adjutant, Commander, Director, Deputy Director, and Squad Leader;
translations.idiomatic: squads had Chief Adjutant, Commander, Director, Deputy Director, and Squad Leader;

sentences.zh: 御龍諸直有四直都虞候，本直各有都虞候、指揮使、副指揮使、都頭、副都頭、十將、將虞候；

translations.literal: Imperial Dragon direct squads had four direct Chief Adjutants; each direct squad had Chief Adjutant, Commander, Deputy Commander, Squad Head, Deputy Squad Head, Ten-Captain, and Captain Adjutant;
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Dragon direct squads had four direct Chief Adjutants; each direct squad had Chief Adjutant, Commander, Deputy Commander, Squad Head, Deputy Squad Head, Ten-Captain, and Captain Adjutant;

sentences.zh: 馬步軍有捧日、天武左右四廂都指揮使，捧日、天武左右各有都指揮使，每軍有都指揮使、都虞候，每指揮有指揮使、副指揮使，每都有軍使、步軍謂之都頭。

translations.literal: mounted and foot armies had Sun-Holding and Heavenly Martial left and right four-wing Overall Commanders; Sun-Holding and Heavenly Martial left and right each had Overall Commanders; each army had Overall Commander and Chief Adjutant; each command had Commander and Deputy Commander; each company had Army Commissioner—in infantry called Squad Head.
translations.idiomatic: mounted and foot armies had Sun-Holding and Heavenly Martial left and right four-wing Overall Commanders; Sun-Holding and Heavenly Martial left and right each had Overall Commanders; each army had Overall Commander and Chief Adjutant; each command had Commander and Deputy Commander; each company had Army Commissioner—in infantry called Squad Head.

sentences.zh: 副兵馬使、步軍謂之副都頭。

translations.literal: Deputy Army Commissioner—in infantry called Deputy Squad Head.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy Army Commissioner—in infantry called Deputy Squad Head.

sentences.zh: 十將、將虞候、承局、押官。

translations.literal: Ten-Captain, Captain Adjutant, Clerk, and Escort Officer.
translations.idiomatic: Ten-Captain, Captain Adjutant, Clerk, and Escort Officer.

sentences.zh: 所領諸班直、指揮，騎兵、步兵之額敘列如左。

translations.literal: The quotas of cavalry and infantry in the various squad-direct commands and units are set forth below.
translations.idiomatic: The cavalry and infantry quotas of the various squad-direct commands and units are set forth below.

sentences.zh: 以其前後之異同者分爲建隆以來之制、熙寧以後之制，而將兵、水兵之制可考者，因附著於後雲。

translations.literal: Because earlier and later arrangements differ, they are divided into the system since Jianlong and the system after Xining; verifiable arrangements for commander troops and naval troops are appended afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Because earlier and later arrangements differ, they are divided into the system since Jianlong and the system after Xining; verifiable arrangements for commander troops and naval troops are appended afterward.

sentences.zh: 建隆以來之制

translations.literal: The system since Jianlong
translations.idiomatic: The system since Jianlong

sentences.zh: 殿前指揮使左右班二。

translations.literal: Palace Front Commander left and right squads, two.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Front Commander left and right squads, two.

sentences.zh: 宋初，以舊府親從帶甲之士及諸班軍騎中選武藝絕倫者充。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, men were chosen from the old headquarters' armored personal followers and from various squad cavalry for unmatched martial skill.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Song, men were chosen from the old headquarters' armored personal followers and from various squad cavalries for unmatched martial skill.

sentences.zh: 內殿直左右班四。

translations.literal: Inner Hall Direct left and right squads, four.
translations.idiomatic: Inner Hall Direct left and right squads, four.

sentences.zh: 周制，簡軍校暨武臣子弟有材勇者立。

translations.literal: Under the Zhou system, established by selecting military officers and martial sons of officials with talent and courage.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou system, established by selecting military officers and martial sons of officials with talent and courage.

sentences.zh: 又有川班內殿直，乾德三年平蜀得奇兵，簡閱材貌魁偉便習騎射者凡百二十人立，開寶四年廢。

translations.literal: There was also Sichuan Squad Inner Hall Direct: in the third year of Qiande, after pacifying Shu, odd troops were obtained; one hundred twenty men of imposing build skilled in mounted archery were selected and established; abolished in the fourth year of Kaibao.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Sichuan Squad Inner Hall Direct: in Qiande 3, after pacifying Shu, exceptional troops were taken; one hundred twenty men of imposing build skilled in mounted archery were selected and established; abolished in Kaibao 4.

sentences.zh: 散員左右班四。

translations.literal: Loose Members left and right squads, four.
translations.idiomatic: Loose Members left and right squads, four.

sentences.zh: 周制，招置諸州豪傑立，散指揮、散都頭、散祗候凡十二班。

translations.literal: Under the Zhou system, established by recruiting heroes from the various prefectures; Loose Commands, Loose Squad Leaders, and Loose Attendants totaled twelve squads.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou system, established by recruiting heroes from the various prefectures; Loose Commands, Loose Squad Leaders, and Loose Attendants totaled twelve squads.

sentences.zh: 又於北面驍捷員僚直及諸軍內簡閱填補。

translations.literal: Men were also selected from the Northern Fierce Swift Officer Direct and from among the various armies to fill vacancies.
translations.idiomatic: Men were also selected from the Northern Fierce Swift Officer Direct and from among the various armies to fill vacancies.

sentences.zh: 咸平五年，定州路都部署王超言；

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianping, Dingzhou Route Overall Deployment Wang Chao memorialized;
translations.idiomatic: In Xianping 5, Dingzhou Route Overall Deployment Wang Chao memorialized;

sentences.zh: 「緣邊有強梁輩常居四界，擾動邊境，請厚給金帛募充散員。

translations.literal: "On the frontier there are strongmen who constantly dwell in the border zones and disturb the frontier—we beg to recruit them generously with gold and silk as Loose Members.
translations.idiomatic: "On the frontier there are strongmen who constantly dwell in the border zones and disturb the frontier—we ask to recruit them generously with gold and silk as Loose Members.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " Approval was given.
translations.idiomatic: " Approval was given.

sentences.zh: 散指揮左右班四。

translations.literal: Loose Commands left and right squads, four.
translations.idiomatic: Loose Commands left and right squads, four.

sentences.zh: 散都頭左右班二。

translations.literal: Loose Squad Leaders left and right squads, two.
translations.idiomatic: Loose Squad Leaders left and right squads, two.

sentences.zh: 金槍班左右班二，舊名內直。

translations.literal: Golden Spear squads left and right, two; formerly called Inner Direct.
translations.idiomatic: Golden Spear squads left and right, two; formerly called Inner Direct.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，改選諸軍中善用槍槊者補之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo, men skilled with spear and halberd were selected from the various armies to fill them.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo, men skilled with spear and halberd were selected from the various armies to fill them.

sentences.zh: 東西班弩手、龍旗直、招箭班共十二，舊號東西班承旨。

translations.literal: East and West Squad crossbowmen, Dragon Banner Direct, and Arrow Summons Squad totaled twelve; formerly called East and West Squad Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: East and West Squad crossbowmen, Dragon Banner Direct, and Arrow Summons Squad totaled twelve; formerly called East and West Squad Attendants.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年，改爲殿前侍，東西各第一第二弩手、龍旗直班六，並帶甲，選諸班及不帶甲班增補。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua, it was changed to Palace Front Attendants; east and west each had first and second crossbowmen and Dragon Banner Direct squads, six in all, all armored; selected from various squads and unarmored squads to fill vacancies.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunhua 2, the unit became Palace Front Attendants: six armored squads—east and west first and second crossbowmen plus Dragon Banner Direct—filled from other squads and unarmored squads.

sentences.zh: 其東第二茶酒及第三、西第四班不帶甲，並以諸軍員、使臣及沒王事者子弟爲之。

translations.literal: Its east second Tea-and-Wine squad and third, and west fourth squads were unarmored; all were staffed by sons of army officers, imperial envoys, and those who died in imperial service.
translations.idiomatic: The east second Tea-and-Wine and third squads and the west fourth squad wore no armor; their ranks came from army officers' sons, envoys' sons, and sons of men who had died in imperial service.

sentences.zh: 又擇善弓箭者爲招箭班。

translations.literal: Skilled archers were also selected for the Arrow Summons Squad.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled archers were also chosen for the Arrow Summons Squad.

sentences.zh: 散直左右班四。

translations.literal: Loose Direct left and right squads, four.
translations.idiomatic: Loose Direct left and right squads, four.

sentences.zh: 雍熙四年，以諸道募置藩鎮廳頭軍將及詣登聞院求試武藝者立。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongxi, established from circuit-recruited frontier command hall-head military officers and those who went to the Direct Petition Court to request trials of martial skill.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi 4, it was established from frontier hall-head officers recruited on the circuits and from men who petitioned at the Direct Petition Court to test their martial skill.

sentences.zh: 咸平元年，選諸節度使從人、騎御馬小底增補。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianping, selected from military commissioners' attendants and Imperial Mount Junior Attendants to fill vacancies.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianping 1, vacancies were filled from military commissioners' attendants and Imperial Mount Junior Attendants.

sentences.zh: 鈞容直班二。

translations.literal: Imperial Procession Direct squads, two.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Procession Direct squads, two.

sentences.zh: 太平興國三年，選諸軍諳曉音樂、騎御馬小底立。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiping Xingguo, established by selecting from various armies those skilled in music and Imperial Mount Junior Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 3, it was established from troops in various armies who knew music and from Imperial Mount Junior Attendants.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年，改之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua, it was changed.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunhua 2, it was reorganized.

sentences.zh: 外殿直班一。

translations.literal: Outer Hall Direct squad, one.
translations.idiomatic: Outer Hall Direct squad, one.

sentences.zh: 諸班衛士中年多者號看班外殿直，後削看班之號。

translations.literal: Among squad guards, those of advanced age were called Watch-Squad Outer Hall Direct; later the Watch-Squad designation was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Older squad guards were called Watch-Squad Outer Hall Direct; later the Watch-Squad title was dropped.

sentences.zh: 或詣諸道攝軍校之職部分州兵，謂之權管。

translations.literal: Some would go to various circuits to act in the capacity of military officers and divide prefectural troops—called Provisional Command.
translations.idiomatic: Some were sent to circuits to serve temporarily as military officers and take charge of prefectural troops—called Provisional Command.

sentences.zh: 國初又有內員僚直，開寶中廢。

translations.literal: At the founding there was also Inner Officer Direct; abolished in the Kaibao era.
translations.idiomatic: At the dynasty's founding there was also Inner Officer Direct; it was abolished under Kaibao.

sentences.zh: 太平興國四年，征太原，得上軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo, in the campaign against Taiyuan, superior troops were obtained.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 4, campaigning against Taiyuan, superior troops were obtained.

sentences.zh: 天禧四年，併入此班。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianxi, merged into this squad.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianxi 4, it was merged into this squad.

sentences.zh: 捧日並左射、钅屈直、弩手、左第五軍，總指揮三十五。

translations.literal: Sun-Holding together with Left Shooter, Bent Bow Direct, crossbowmen, and Left Fifth Army—thirty-five commands in all.
translations.idiomatic: Sun-Holding, Left Shooter, Bent Bow Direct, crossbowmen, and Left Fifth Army—thirty-five commands in all.

sentences.zh: 京師三十三，雍丘、鄭各一。

translations.literal: Thirty-three at the capital; Yongqiu and Zheng one each.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-three at the capital; one each at Yongqiu and Zheng.

sentences.zh: 舊號小底，周改爲鐵騎，太平興國二年改爲日騎，雍熙四年改今名。

translations.literal: Formerly called Junior Attendants; under Zhou changed to Iron Cavalry; in the second year of Taiping Xingguo changed to Sun Cavalry; in the fourth year of Yongxi changed to the present name.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Junior Attendants; under Zhou renamed Iron Cavalry; in Taiping Xingguo 2 Sun Cavalry; in Yongxi 4 given its present name.

sentences.zh: 分左、右廂，各四軍。

translations.literal: Divided into left and right wings, four armies each.
translations.idiomatic: It was divided into left and right wings of four armies each.

sentences.zh: 雍熙三年，選善槍槊者充钅屈直。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi, skilled spearmen were selected to fill Bent Bow Direct.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi 3, skilled spearmen were chosen for Bent Bow Direct.

sentences.zh: 淳化三年，選善左射者爲左射。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chunhua, skilled left shooters were selected for Left Shooter.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunhua 3, skilled left shooters were chosen for Left Shooter.

sentences.zh: 咸平五年，選天武、拱聖、驍騎善弩射者爲弩手。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianping, skilled crossbowmen from Heavenly Martial, Bowing to the Stars, and Fierce Cavalry were selected as crossbowmen.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianping 5, skilled crossbowmen were drawn from Heavenly Martial, Bowing to the Stars, and Fierce Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 契丹直三。

translations.literal: Khitan Direct, three.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan Direct, three.

sentences.zh: 咸平、許、壽各一。

translations.literal: Xianping, Xu, and Shou one each.
translations.idiomatic: One each at Xianping, Xu, and Shou.

sentences.zh: 後唐置，旋廢。

translations.literal: Established under Later Tang, soon abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Established under Later Tang and soon abolished.

sentences.zh: 開寶三年，以遼人內附之衆復置。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaibao, re-established with Liao people who had submitted.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaibao 3, it was re-established with Liao subjects who had defected inward.

sentences.zh: 太平興國中，因事復置，旋廢。

translations.literal: In the Taiping Xingguo era, re-established on account of events, soon abolished.
translations.idiomatic: During Taiping Xingguo it was briefly re-established, then abolished again.

sentences.zh: 歸明渤海指揮二。

translations.literal: Surrendered Ming Bohai commands, two.
translations.idiomatic: Surrendered Ming Bohai commands, two.

sentences.zh: 京師。

translations.literal: The capital.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital.

sentences.zh: 太平興國四年，征幽州，以渤海降兵立。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo, in the campaign against Youzhou, established with Bohai surrendered troops.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 4, campaigning against Youzhou, it was established from surrendered Bohai troops.

sentences.zh: 拱聖指揮二十一。

translations.literal: Bowing to the Stars commands, twenty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Bowing to the Stars commands, twenty-one.

sentences.zh: 京師。

translations.literal: The capital.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital.

sentences.zh: 乾德中，選諸州騎兵送闕下，立爲驍雄，後改驍猛。

translations.literal: During Qiande, cavalry from various prefectures sent to court were established as Fierce Bold; later changed to Fierce Fierce.
translations.idiomatic: During Qiande, prefectural cavalry sent to court formed Fierce Bold; later renamed Fierce Fierce.

sentences.zh: 雍熙四年，又改拱辰。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongxi, again changed to Bowing to the Stars.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi 4, it was renamed again Bowing to the Stars.

sentences.zh: 未幾改今名。

translations.literal: Before long changed to the present name.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward it received its present name.

sentences.zh: 吐渾小底舊指揮五，治平中並爲二。

translations.literal: Tujue Junior Attendants formerly five commands; in the Zhiping era merged to two.
translations.idiomatic: Tujue Junior Attendants formerly had five commands; in the Zhiping era they were merged into two.

sentences.zh: 京師。

translations.literal: The capital.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital.

sentences.zh: 太平興國四年，平太原，獲吐渾子弟，又選監牧諸軍中所有者充。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo, after pacifying Taiyuan, Tujue youths were obtained; also selected from those in pasture-supervision armies to fill.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 4, after the pacification of Taiyuan, Tujue youths were taken in; men from pasture-supervision armies were also selected to fill the ranks.

sentences.zh: 驍騎指揮二十三。

translations.literal: Fierce Cavalry commands, twenty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce Cavalry commands, twenty-three.

sentences.zh: 京師。

translations.literal: The capital.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital.

sentences.zh: 太平興國四年置，後又選掉搨索兵及左右教駿兵增置。

translations.literal: Established in the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo; later also increased by selecting Rope Handler troops and Left and Right Training Steeds troops.
translations.idiomatic: Established in Taiping Xingguo 4; later expanded by drawing on Rope Handler troops and the Left and Right Training Steeds.

sentences.zh: 雍熙四年，改殿前司步鬥弩手爲驍騎弩手。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongxi, Palace Front Bureau Foot Combat crossbowmen were changed to Fierce Cavalry crossbowmen.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi 4, the Palace Front Bureau's Foot Combat crossbowmen became Fierce Cavalry crossbowmen.

sentences.zh: 淳化四年，選壯勇超絕者爲上驍騎，在本軍之上。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chunhua, exceptionally stalwart and courageous men were selected as Upper Fierce Cavalry, above the main army.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunhua 4, the strongest and boldest were chosen as Upper Fierce Cavalry, ranking above the main force.

sentences.zh: 咸平五年，分左、右廂。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianping, divided into left and right wings.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianping 5, it was split into left and right wings.

sentences.zh: 舊又有殿前小底。

translations.literal: Formerly there was also Palace Front Junior Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: There had also been Palace Front Junior Attendants.

sentences.zh: 至道二年，選驍騎馬直及善射者充，後廢。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhidao, selected from Fierce Cavalry Horse Direct and skilled archers to fill; later abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhidao 2, it was filled from Fierce Cavalry Horse Direct and skilled archers; later abolished.

sentences.zh: 驍勝左右指揮各五。

translations.literal: Fierce Victory left and right commands, five each.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce Victory left and right commands, five each.

sentences.zh: 京師。

translations.literal: The capital.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital.

sentences.zh: 咸平三年，選教駿、驍騎諸軍備征子弟材勇者立。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianping, established by selecting sons of Training Steeds and Fierce Cavalry Campaign Ready armies with talent and courage.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianping 3, it was established from talented, courageous sons of Training Steeds and Fierce Cavalry Campaign Ready troops.

sentences.zh: 甯朔指揮十。

translations.literal: Secure the North commands, ten.
translations.idiomatic: Secure the North commands, ten.

sentences.zh: 京師、尉氏各三，雍丘、渭、河陽、河陰各一。

translations.literal: Capital and Weishi three each; Yongqiu, Wei, Heyang, and Heyin one each.
translations.idiomatic: Three each at the capital and Weishi; one each at Yongqiu, Wei, Heyang, and Heyin.

sentences.zh: 咸平三年，選教駿諸軍備征及外州兵立。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianping, established by selecting from Training Steeds Campaign Ready armies and outlying prefecture troops.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianping 3, it was established from Training Steeds Campaign Ready troops and troops from outlying prefectures.

sentences.zh: 龍猛指揮八。

translations.literal: Dragon Fierce commands, eight.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon Fierce commands, eight.

sentences.zh: 京師。

translations.literal: The capital.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital.

sentences.zh: 太平興國中，揀閱龍騎及諸州部送招獲群盜，取其材勇者立。

translations.literal: In the Taiping Xingguo era, Dragon Cavalry and bandits captured and escorted from various prefectures were reviewed; the talented and courageous were selected to establish it.
translations.idiomatic: During Taiping Xingguo, Dragon Cavalry and captured bandits escorted from the prefectures were reviewed, and the ablest and boldest were chosen to form the unit.

sentences.zh: 淳化四年，又擇精悍者爲教閱龍猛以備禽盜，在本軍之上。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chunhua, elite fierce men were selected as Training-Review Dragon Fierce to prepare for capturing bandits, above the main army.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunhua 4, picked elite formed Training-Review Dragon Fierce to hunt bandits, ranking above the main force.

sentences.zh: 景德四年，又選龍騎、驍騎兵增之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jingde, Dragon Cavalry and Fierce Cavalry troops were also selected to increase it.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingde 4, Dragon Cavalry and Fierce Cavalry troops were added to enlarge it.

sentences.zh: 飛猛指揮二。

translations.literal: Flying Fierce commands, two.
translations.idiomatic: Flying Fierce commands, two.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年，選龍猛、驍騎兵子弟之材勇者立。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping, established by selecting sons of Dragon Fierce and Fierce Cavalry troops with talent and courage.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianping 2, it was established from talented, courageous sons of Dragon Fierce and Fierce Cavalry troops.

sentences.zh: 驍猛指揮四。

translations.literal: Fierce Bold commands, four.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce Bold commands, four.

sentences.zh: 尉氏三、太康一。

translations.literal: Weishi three, Taikang one.
translations.idiomatic: Three at Weishi, one at Taikang.

sentences.zh: 舊號驍雄，太平興國中改。

translations.literal: Formerly called Fierce Bold; changed in the Taiping Xingguo era.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Fierce Bold; renamed during Taiping Xingguo.

sentences.zh: 雍熙四年，以拱聖年多者爲拱辰軍，其次等者如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongxi, the oldest in Bowing to the Stars were made Bowing to the Stars Army; those of secondary grade remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi 4, the oldest Bowing to the Stars troops became Bowing to the Stars Army; those of the next grade stayed where they were.

sentences.zh: 景德四年，以拱聖年多者隸之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jingde, the oldest in Bowing to the Stars were attached to it.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingde 4, the oldest Bowing to the Stars troops were transferred to it.

sentences.zh: 神騎指揮十八。

translations.literal: Divine Cavalry commands, eighteen.
translations.idiomatic: Divine Cavalry commands, eighteen.

sentences.zh: 雍丘十三，咸平五。

translations.literal: Yongqiu thirteen, Xianping five.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen at Yongqiu, five at Xianping.

sentences.zh: 端拱二年，選驍雄新配人及教駿、借事等兵立。

translations.literal: In the second year of Duangong, established by selecting newly assigned Fierce Bold men and Training Steeds, Temporary Duty, and other troops.
translations.idiomatic: In Duangong 2, it was established from newly assigned Fierce Bold men plus Training Steeds, Temporary Duty, and other troops.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年，廢掉搨索軍隸之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua, the Rope Handler army was abolished and attached to it.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunhua 2, the Rope Handler army was abolished and absorbed into it.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年，又擇教駿、備征及外州增之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping, Training Steeds, Campaign Ready, and outlying prefectures were again selected to increase it.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianping 2, more men were added from Training Steeds, Campaign Ready, and outlying prefectures.

sentences.zh: 驍雄指揮四。

translations.literal: Fierce Bold commands, four.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce Bold commands, four.

sentences.zh: 咸平、陳留各二。

translations.literal: Xianping and Chenliu two each.
translations.idiomatic: Two each at Xianping and Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 太平興國八年，遷驍猛中次等者立。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Taiping Xingguo, those of secondary grade from Fierce Bold were transferred to establish it.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 8, second-grade men from Fierce Bold were transferred to form it.

sentences.zh: 景德中，以驍騎、驍勝、寧朔軍年多者隸之。

translations.literal: In the Jingde era, the oldest from Fierce Cavalry, Fierce Victory, and Secure the North armies were attached to it.
translations.idiomatic: During Jingde, the oldest troops from Fierce Cavalry, Fierce Victory, and Secure the North were assigned to it.

sentences.zh: 吐渾直指揮三。

translations.literal: Tujue Direct commands, three.
translations.idiomatic: Tujue Direct commands, three.

sentences.zh: 太原二，潞一。

translations.literal: Taiyuan two, Lu one.
translations.idiomatic: Two at Taiyuan, one at Lu.

sentences.zh: 太平興國八年，太原遷雲州及河界吐渾立，屯並、代州。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Taiping Xingguo, established with Tujue relocated from Taiyuan, Yun Prefecture, and the Yellow River frontier; garrisoned at Bing and Dai prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 8, it was formed from Tujue relocated from Taiyuan, Yun Prefecture, and the Yellow River frontier and garrisoned at Bing and Dai.

sentences.zh: 雍熙三年，又得雲、朔歸明吐渾增立，屯潞州。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi, surrendered Ming Tujue from Yun and Shuo were also obtained to add and establish; garrisoned at Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi 3, more surrendered Ming Tujue from Yun and Shuo were added; the unit was garrisoned at Lu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 安慶直四。

translations.literal: Secure Celebration Direct, four.
translations.idiomatic: Secure Celebration Direct, four.

sentences.zh: 太原一，潞三。

translations.literal: Taiyuan one, Lu three.
translations.idiomatic: One at Taiyuan, three at Lu.

sentences.zh: 太平興國四年，遷雲、朔及河東歸明安慶民分屯並、潞等州，給以土田。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo, surrendered Ming Secure Celebration people from Yun, Shuo, and Hedong were relocated; stationed separately at Bing, Lu, and other prefectures and granted land.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 4, surrendered Ming Secure Celebration people from Yun, Shuo, and Hedong were resettled at Bing, Lu, and other prefectures and given land.

sentences.zh: 雍熙四年立。

translations.literal: Established in the fourth year of Yongxi.
translations.idiomatic: Established in Yongxi 4.

sentences.zh: 三部落指揮一。

translations.literal: Three Tribes commands, one.
translations.idiomatic: Three Tribes commands, one.

sentences.zh: 太原。

translations.literal: Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: At Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 太平興國四年，親征幽州，遷雲、朔、應等州部落於并州，因立。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo, in the personal campaign against Youzhou, tribes from Yun, Shuo, Ying, and other prefectures were relocated to Bing Prefecture and thus established.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 4, on the emperor's campaign against Youzhou, tribes from Yun, Shuo, Ying, and other prefectures were moved to Bing Prefecture and the command was established.

sentences.zh: 清朔指揮四。

translations.literal: Clear North commands, four.
translations.idiomatic: Clear North commands, four.

sentences.zh: 西京二，許、汝各一。

translations.literal: Western Capital two; Xu and Ru one each.
translations.idiomatic: Two at the Western Capital; one each at Xu and Ru.

sentences.zh: 太平興國四年，遷雲、朔州民於內地，得自置馬以爲騎兵，謂之家戶馬。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo, people of Yun and Shuo prefectures were relocated inland; allowed to provide their own horses as cavalry—called Household Horse.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 4, people from Yun and Shuo were resettled inland, allowed to supply their own horses as cavalry—these were called Household Horse troops.

sentences.zh: 雍熙四年立。

translations.literal: Established in the fourth year of Yongxi.
translations.idiomatic: Established in Yongxi 4.

sentences.zh: 擒戎指揮五。

translations.literal: Capture Barbarians commands, five.
translations.idiomatic: Capture Barbarians commands, five.

sentences.zh: 西京、許各二，汝一。

translations.literal: Western Capital and Xu two each; Ru one.
translations.idiomatic: Two each at the Western Capital and Xu; one at Ru.

sentences.zh: 太平興國四年，遷雲、朔州民於西京、許汝等州，給以土田，充家戶馬。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo, people of Yun and Shuo prefectures were relocated to Western Capital, Xu, Ru, and other prefectures; granted land and filled as Household Horse.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 4, people from Yun and Shuo were resettled at the Western Capital, Xu, Ru, and other prefectures, given land, and enrolled as Household Horse troops.

sentences.zh: 端拱二年立。

translations.literal: Established in the second year of Duangong.
translations.idiomatic: Established in Duangong 2.

sentences.zh: 新安內員僚直五。

translations.literal: Xin'an Inner Officer Direct, five.
translations.idiomatic: Xin'an Inner Officer Direct, five.

sentences.zh: 端拱二年，成德軍節度使田重進言；

translations.literal: In the second year of Duangong, Chengde Army Military Commissioner Tian Chongjin memorialized;
translations.idiomatic: In Duangong 2, Chengde Army Military Commissioner Tian Chongjin memorialized;

sentences.zh: 「易州靜砦兵先屯鎮州，賊陷勇陷穀，盡俘其家，請以其軍備宿衛。

translations.literal: "The Jingzhai troops of Yi Prefecture had been stationed at Zhen Prefecture; bandits captured Yongxiangu and took all their families captive—we request that this army serve as palace guard reserve.
translations.idiomatic: "The Jingzhai troops of Yi Prefecture had been posted at Zhen Prefecture; when bandits seized Yongxiangu they captured every man's family. We ask that this army be kept as palace guard reserve.

sentences.zh: 」因而立此直。

translations.literal: " Thus this Direct was established.
translations.idiomatic: " The Direct was established on that basis.

sentences.zh: 後廢，天聖後無。

translations.literal: Later abolished; none after Tiansheng.
translations.idiomatic: It was later abolished and did not exist after Tiansheng.

sentences.zh: 散祗候左右班二。

translations.literal: Loose Attendants left and right squads, two.
translations.idiomatic: Loose Attendants left and right squads, two.

sentences.zh: 天聖前無。

translations.literal: None before Tiansheng.
translations.idiomatic: It did not exist before Tiansheng.

sentences.zh: 步鬥指揮六。

translations.literal: Foot Combat commands, six.
translations.idiomatic: Foot Combat commands, six.

sentences.zh: 尉氏、太康各一，蔡四。

translations.literal: Weishi and Taikang, one each; Cai, four.
translations.idiomatic: One command each at Weishi and Taikang; four at Cai.

sentences.zh: 慶曆中增置，天聖前無。

translations.literal: Added during Qingli; none before Tiansheng.
translations.idiomatic: These were added during the Qingli era; before Tiansheng there were none.

sentences.zh: 御龍直左右二。

translations.literal: Imperial Dragon Direct, left and right, two.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Dragon Direct: two commands, left and right.

sentences.zh: 舊號簇御馬直，太平興國二年改爲簇御龍直，後改今名。

translations.literal: Formerly called Clustered Imperial Horse Direct; in the second year of Taiping Xingguo changed to Clustered Imperial Dragon Direct; later given the present name.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Clustered Imperial Horse Direct; in Taiping Xingguo 2 renamed Clustered Imperial Dragon Direct, and later given its present name.

sentences.zh: 御龍骨朵子直左右二。

translations.literal: Imperial Dragon Mace Direct, left and right, two.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Dragon Mace Direct: two commands, left and right.

sentences.zh: 舊號骨䤪子直，太平興國二年改爲御龍散手直，後改今名。

translations.literal: Formerly called Bone Mace Direct; in the second year of Taiping Xingguo changed to Imperial Dragon Loose-Hand Direct; later given the present name.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Bone Mace Direct; in Taiping Xingguo 2 renamed Imperial Dragon Loose-Hand Direct, and later given its present name.

sentences.zh: 御龍弓箭直五。

translations.literal: Imperial Dragon Bow Direct, five.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Dragon Bow Direct: five commands.

sentences.zh: 選天武諸軍材貌魁傑者充。

translations.literal: Men of outstanding physique and appearance were selected from among the Heavenly Martial armies to fill the posts.
translations.idiomatic: Filled from the Heavenly Martial armies with men of outstanding build and bearing.

sentences.zh: 御龍弩直五。

translations.literal: Imperial Dragon Crossbow Direct, five.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Dragon Crossbow Direct: five commands.

sentences.zh: 天武並寬衣、钅屈直、左射，總指揮三十四。

translations.literal: Heavenly Martial, together with Loose-Robe, Bent Bow Direct, and Left Shooter—thirty-four commands in all.
translations.idiomatic: Heavenly Martial together with Loose-Robe, Bent Bow Direct, and Left Shooter units: thirty-four commands in all.

sentences.zh: 京師三十三，咸平一。

translations.literal: Thirty-three in the capital; one at Xianping.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-three in the capital and one at Xianping.

sentences.zh: 神勇上下共二十一指揮。

translations.literal: Divine Courage, upper and lower, twenty-one commands in all.
translations.idiomatic: Divine Courage, upper and lower ranks: twenty-one commands in all.

sentences.zh: 乾德中，揀閱諸軍壯實而大體者立爲雄威。

translations.literal: In Qiande, sturdy men of large build were selected from among the various armies and formed as Bold Prestige.
translations.idiomatic: In Qiande, the sturdiest and largest men from the various armies were reviewed and formed into Bold Prestige.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，改爲雄勇。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo, renamed Bold Courage.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 2 it was renamed Bold Courage.

sentences.zh: 雍熙四年改今名。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongxi, given the present name.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi 4 it received its present name, Divine Courage.

sentences.zh: 淳化四年，選武藝超絕者立爲上神勇，以備擒盜。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chunhua, men of surpassing martial skill were selected and formed as Upper Divine Courage, to capture bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunhua 4, men of surpassing martial skill were chosen to form Upper Divine Courage, a unit kept ready to hunt down bandits.

sentences.zh: 宣武上下共二十指揮。

translations.literal: Xuanwu, upper and lower, twenty commands in all.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanwu, upper and lower ranks: twenty commands in all.

sentences.zh: 京師。

translations.literal: The capital.
translations.idiomatic: Stationed in the capital.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，並效節、忠猛二軍立，又選諸軍及鄉兵增之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo, established together with the Render Obedience and Loyal Fierce armies; men were also selected from various armies and the Local Militia to augment it.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 2 it was raised together with the Render Obedience and Loyal Fierce armies, then augmented with picks from other armies and the Local Militia.

sentences.zh: 至道二年，又選軍頭司步直善用槍槊掉刀者立殿前步直，後廢。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhidao, men skilled with spear, halberd, and dao from the Army Head Bureau foot direct were selected to form Palace Front Foot Direct; later abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhidao 2, spear-, halberd-, and dao-men from the Army Head Bureau foot direct were chosen to form Palace Front Foot Direct; the unit was later abolished.

sentences.zh: 虎翼太平興國中，揀雄武弩手立爲上鐵林，又于雄武、定遠、寧勝床子弩手、飛山雄武等軍選勁兵以增其數。

translations.literal: Tiger Wing: in Taiping Xingguo, Bold Martial crossbowmen were selected to form Upper Iron Forest; strong soldiers were also chosen from Bold Martial, Secure Distance, Secure Victory bed-frame crossbow units, Flying Mountain Bold Martial, and other armies to increase its numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Tiger Wing: during Taiping Xingguo, Bold Martial crossbowmen were formed into Upper Iron Forest, and crack troops were drawn from Bold Martial, Secure Distance, Secure Victory bed-frame crossbow units, Flying Mountain Bold Martial, and other commands to swell its ranks.

sentences.zh: 雍熙四年，改分左右四軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongxi, reorganized into left and right, four armies.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi 4 it was split into left and right wings, four armies in all.

sentences.zh: 淳化四年，選本軍精銳者爲上虎翼，以備禽盜。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chunhua, elite men from the army were selected as Upper Tiger Wing, to capture bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunhua 4, the army's best men were picked for Upper Tiger Wing, kept ready to hunt down bandits.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年，並廣勇軍隸之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping, the Broad Courage army was merged under it.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianping 2 the Broad Courage army was absorbed into it.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符六年，詔在京諸軍選江、淮士卒善水者習戰于金明池，立爲虎翼水軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, an edict ordered units in the capital to select Yangtze-Huai soldiers skilled in water to drill at Jinming Pool and form them as Tiger Wing Navy.
translations.idiomatic: In Dazhong Xiangfu 6, an edict directed capital units to choose Yangtze-Huai men skilled on the water, drill them at Jinming Pool, and form Tiger Wing Navy.

sentences.zh: 舊指揮六十二，景德中增六。

translations.literal: Formerly sixty-two commands; six added in Jingde.
translations.idiomatic: It had formerly numbered sixty-two commands; six were added in the Jingde era.

sentences.zh: 京師。

translations.literal: The capital.
translations.idiomatic: Stationed in the capital.

sentences.zh: 雄勇舊號雄威，太平興國二年改今名。

translations.literal: Bold Courage was formerly called Bold Prestige; in the second year of Taiping Xingguo renamed to the present name.
translations.idiomatic: Bold Courage had formerly been Bold Prestige; in Taiping Xingguo 2 it received its present name.

sentences.zh: 雍熙四年，改神勇，復於本軍選退入次等者爲之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongxi, renamed Divine Courage; men who had fallen to second tier were again selected from within the army.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi 4 it was renamed Divine Courage, and men who had slipped to second rank within the army were chosen again to fill it.

sentences.zh: 舊指揮五，至和五年增爲八。

translations.literal: Formerly five commands; in the fifth year of Zhihe increased to eight.
translations.idiomatic: It had formerly stood at five commands; in Zhihe 5 the total rose to eight.

sentences.zh: 咸平三，鄆二，許、鄭、滑各一。

translations.literal: Three at Xianping; two at Yun; one each at Xu, Zheng, and Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Three at Xianping; two at Yun; one each at Xu, Zheng, and Hua.

sentences.zh: 廣德開寶四年，平廣南，以其兵隸殿前司，次等隸八作司，闕則選廣南諸州兵補之。

translations.literal: Broad Virtue: in the fourth year of Kaibao, when Guangnan was pacified, its troops were assigned to the Palace Front Bureau; second-tier men to the Eight Works Bureau; vacancies were filled by selecting troops from Guangnan prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Broad Virtue: in Kaibao 4, after Guangnan was pacified, its troops entered the Palace Front Bureau, second-tier men went to the Eight Works Bureau, and gaps were filled from Guangnan prefectural forces.

sentences.zh: 雍熙三年，選八作司之強壯者爲揀中。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi, strong men from the Eight Works Bureau were selected as Selected.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi 3, the strongest men in the Eight Works Bureau were chosen for Selected Broad Virtue.

sentences.zh: 總指揮十。

translations.literal: Ten commands in all.
translations.idiomatic: Ten commands in all.

sentences.zh: 咸平、尉氏、陽武、河陽、滄、鞏、白波各一，西京三。

translations.literal: One each at Xianping, Weishi, Yangwu, Heyang, Cang, Gong, and Baibo; three at the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: One command each at Xianping, Weishi, Yangwu, Heyang, Cang, Gong, and Baibo; three at the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 廣勇淳化二年，選神射、鞭箭、雄武、效忠等軍強壯善射者立爲廣武，大中祥符二年改今名。

translations.literal: Broad Courage: in the second year of Chunhua, strong archers were selected from Divine Archer, Whip Arrow, Bold Martial, Render Loyalty, and other armies to form Broad Martial; in the second year of Dazhong Xiangfu renamed to the present name.
translations.idiomatic: Broad Courage: in Chunhua 2, strong bowmen were taken from Divine Archer, Whip Arrow, Bold Martial, Render Loyalty, and other units to form Broad Martial; in Dazhong Xiangfu 2 it received its present name.

sentences.zh: 舊指揮二十三，慶曆中增爲四十三，每指揮十爲一軍。

translations.literal: Formerly twenty-three commands; in Qingli increased to forty-three; every ten commands formed one army.
translations.idiomatic: It had formerly numbered twenty-three commands; in Qingli the total rose to forty-three, with every ten commands grouped as one army.

sentences.zh: 京師五，陳留二十二，咸平、東明、太原、胙城、南京各二，襄邑、陽武、鄆各一，滑三。

translations.literal: Five in the capital; twenty-two at Chenliu; two each at Xianping, Dongming, Taiyuan, Zuocheng, and Nanjing; one each at Xiangyi, Yangwu, and Yun; three at Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Five in the capital; twenty-two at Chenliu; two each at Xianping, Dongming, Taiyuan, Zuocheng, and Nanjing; one each at Xiangyi, Yangwu, and Yun; three at Hua.

sentences.zh: 廣捷舊名左右平遠，建隆二年改。

translations.literal: Broad Swift was formerly called Left and Right Level Far; renamed in the second year of Jianlong.
translations.idiomatic: Broad Swift had formerly been Left and Right Level Far; it was renamed in Jianlong 2.

sentences.zh: 咸平五年，又選廣德、神威等軍教以標槍旁牌補之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianping, men from Broad Virtue, Divine Prestige, and other armies were taught pike and side-shield drill and used to fill vacancies.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianping 5, men from Broad Virtue, Divine Prestige, and other commands were drilled in pike and side-shield work and used to fill vacancies.

sentences.zh: 舊指揮五，景祐中增五，明道中增十，慶曆增三十六，總五十六。

translations.literal: Formerly five commands; five added in Jingyou, ten in Mingdao, thirty-six in Qingli—fifty-six in all.
translations.idiomatic: It had begun with five commands; five were added in Jingyou, ten in Mingdao, and thirty-six in Qingli—for fifty-six in all.

sentences.zh: 陳留八，咸平六，雍丘四，襄邑、尉氏、許各三，太康、扶溝、南京、亳、河陰、潁、寧陵各二，陳六，滑、曹、鄧、蔡、廣濟、穀熟、永城、襄城、葉各一。

translations.literal: Eight at Chenliu; six at Xianping; four at Yongqiu; three each at Xiangyi, Weishi, and Xu; two each at Taikang, Fugou, Nanjing, Bo, Heyin, Ying, and Ningling; six at Chen; one each at Hua, Cao, Deng, Cai, Guangji, Gushu, Yongcheng, Xiangcheng, and Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Eight at Chenliu; six at Xianping; four at Yongqiu; three each at Xiangyi, Weishi, and Xu; two each at Taikang, Fugou, Nanjing, Bo, Heyin, Ying, and Ningling; six at Chen; one each at Hua, Cao, Deng, Cai, Guangji, Gushu, Yongcheng, Xiangcheng, and Ye.

sentences.zh: 雄威雍熙四年，選神勇兵退入第二等立爲神威，後改今名。

translations.literal: Bold Prestige: in the fourth year of Yongxi, Divine Courage troops who had fallen to second tier were selected to form Divine Prestige; later given the present name.
translations.idiomatic: Bold Prestige: in Yongxi 4, Divine Courage men who had dropped to second rank were chosen to form Divine Prestige; later it received its present name.

sentences.zh: 指揮十。

translations.literal: Ten commands.
translations.idiomatic: Ten commands.

sentences.zh: 考城、襄邑、陳留各一，南京四，陳二。

translations.literal: One each at Kaocheng, Xiangyi, and Chenliu; four at Nanjing; two at Chen.
translations.idiomatic: One each at Kaocheng, Xiangyi, and Chenliu; four at Nanjing; two at Chen.

sentences.zh: 宣威雍熙四年，選神勇、宣武兵退入次等者立。

translations.literal: Proclaim Prestige: in the fourth year of Yongxi, established from Divine Courage and Xuanwu troops who had fallen to lower tier.
translations.idiomatic: Proclaim Prestige: in Yongxi 4 it was raised from Divine Courage and Xuanwu men who had slipped to lower rank.

sentences.zh: 上下指揮二。

translations.literal: Upper and lower, two commands.
translations.idiomatic: Upper and lower ranks: two commands.

sentences.zh: 咸平、襄邑各一。

translations.literal: One each at Xianping and Xiangyi.
translations.idiomatic: One each at Xianping and Xiangyi.

sentences.zh: 龍騎建隆間以諸道招致及捕獲群寇立，號有馬步人，見陣即步鬥。

translations.literal: Dragon Cavalry: during Jianlong, established by summoning men from various circuits and captives from bandit gangs; called "men with horse and foot"—upon sighting battle they fought on foot.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon Cavalry: during Jianlong it was raised by summoning men from every circuit and captives taken from bandit bands. Known as "horse-and-foot men," they dismounted and fought on foot as soon as they saw the enemy drawn up.

sentences.zh: 淳化三年，選本軍年多者爲帶甲剩員。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chunhua, men of advanced years from the army were selected as Armored Surplus Members.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunhua 3, the army's oldest men were chosen as Armored Surplus Members.

sentences.zh: 咸平以後，又以本軍及龍猛退兵增之。

translations.literal: After Xianping, men retired from the army and from Dragon Fierce were also added to augment it.
translations.idiomatic: After Xianping, retirees from the army itself and from Dragon Fierce were also added to swell its numbers.

sentences.zh: 舊指揮八，康定中，取配隸充軍者增置爲指揮二十，分三軍。

translations.literal: Formerly eight commands; in Kangding, men sentenced to military assignment were taken to expand it to twenty commands, divided into three armies.
translations.idiomatic: It had formerly stood at eight commands; in Kangding, men sentenced to military service were drafted in until it reached twenty commands, divided among three armies.

sentences.zh: 京師四，尉氏、雍丘、咸平、鄭各二，南京、陳、蔡、河陽、潁、單、四波各一。

translations.literal: Four in the capital; two each at Weishi, Yongqiu, Xianping, and Zheng; one each at Nanjing, Chen, Cai, Heyang, Ying, Shan, and Sibo.
translations.idiomatic: Four in the capital; two each at Weishi, Yongqiu, Xianping, and Zheng; one each at Nanjing, Chen, Cai, Heyang, Ying, Shan, and Sibo.

sentences.zh: 步鬥雍熙三年，選諸州廂軍之壯勇者立，後廢。

translations.literal: Foot Combat: in the third year of Yongxi, brave strong men were selected from prefectural Comforter Corps and formed; later abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Foot Combat: in Yongxi 3, brave strong men were chosen from prefectural Comforter Corps and formed into a command; it was later abolished.

sentences.zh: 此下二軍，天聖後無。

translations.literal: The two armies below did not exist after Tiansheng.
translations.idiomatic: The two armies below ceased to exist after the Tiansheng era.

sentences.zh: 鞭箭雍熙三年，選兩浙兵爲鞭箭，次等者爲忠節鞭箭。

translations.literal: Whip Arrow: in the third year of Yongxi, Liang-Zhe troops were selected as Whip Arrow; second-tier men as Loyal Integrity Whip Arrow.
translations.idiomatic: Whip Arrow: in Yongxi 3, Liang-Zhe troops were chosen for Whip Arrow, and second-tier men for Loyal Integrity Whip Arrow.

sentences.zh: 端拱二年並爲一。

translations.literal: In the second year of Duangong, merged into one.
translations.idiomatic: In Duangong 2 the two were merged into one.

sentences.zh: 至道元年，發此兵援靈州芻粟，喪車重兵器於浦洛河，詔免死，後廢。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhidao, these troops were dispatched to escort fodder to Lingzhou; wagons and heavy weapons were lost at the Pulu River; an edict spared them from death; later abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhidao 1 they were sent to convoy fodder to Lingzhou; wagons and heavy weapons were lost at the Pulu River. An edict spared them execution, but the unit was later abolished.

sentences.zh: 侍衛司侍衛親軍馬步軍都指揮使、副都指揮使、都虞候各一人。

translations.literal: Palace Interior Bureau Palace Interior Personal Guard Horse and Foot Armies Overall Commander, Deputy Overall Commander, and Chief Adjutant, one each.
translations.idiomatic: The Palace Interior Bureau had one Overall Commander, one Deputy Overall Commander, and one Chief Adjutant for the Palace Interior Personal Guard Horse and Foot Armies.

sentences.zh: 馬軍都指揮使、副都指揮使、都虞候各一人，步軍亦如之。

translations.literal: Horse Army Overall Commander, Deputy Overall Commander, and Chief Adjutant, one each; the Foot Army likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The Horse Army had one Overall Commander, one Deputy Overall Commander, and one Chief Adjutant; the Foot Army likewise.

sentences.zh: 自馬步軍都虞候已上，其員全闕，即馬、步軍都指揮使等各領其務，與殿前號爲三司。

translations.literal: When the horse-and-foot Chief Adjutant posts and above were entirely vacant, the horse and foot Overall Commanders each managed their own duties, and together with the Palace Front were called the Three Bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chief Adjutant posts and above in the horse-and-foot service stood wholly vacant, the horse and foot Overall Commanders each handled their own affairs, and together with the Palace Front they were called the Three Bureaus.

sentences.zh: 馬步軍有龍衛神衛左右四廂都指揮使、都虞候。

translations.literal: The horse-and-foot armies had Dragon Guard and Divine Guard left and right four-wing Overall Commanders and Chief Adjutants.
translations.idiomatic: The horse-and-foot armies had four-wing Overall Commanders and Chief Adjutants for Dragon Guard and Divine Guard, left and right.

sentences.zh: 每指揮有指揮使、副指揮使。

translations.literal: Each command had a Commander and Deputy Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Each command had a Commander and a Deputy Commander.

sentences.zh: 余如殿前司之制。

translations.literal: The rest followed the Palace Front Bureau system.
translations.idiomatic: All other arrangements followed the Palace Front Bureau model.

sentences.zh: 所領騎兵步兵之額敘列如左：

translations.literal: The quotas of cavalry and infantry under its command are set forth below:
translations.idiomatic: The cavalry and infantry quotas under its command are listed below:

sentences.zh: 員僚直顯德中，周平三關，召募強人及選高陽關馳捷兵爲北面兩直。

translations.literal: Officer Direct: in Xiande, when Zhou pacified the Three Passes, strongmen were recruited and swift troops from Gaoyang Pass were selected to form the two Northern Direct commands.
translations.idiomatic: Officer Direct: in Xiande, when the Zhou pacified the Three Passes, strongmen were recruited and swift troops from Gaoyang Pass were chosen to form the two Northern Direct commands.

sentences.zh: 建隆初，選諸州騎兵及蕃鎮廳頭召募人等爲左三直。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianlong, cavalry from various prefectures and recruitment bureau heads from tribal garrison posts were selected for the three Left Direct commands.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jianlong, prefectural cavalry and recruitment heads from tribal garrison posts were chosen for the three Left Direct commands.

sentences.zh: 太平興國四年，平太原，選其騎兵爲右三直。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taiping Xingguo, when Taiyuan was pacified, its cavalry was selected for the three Right Direct commands.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 4, after Taiyuan fell, its cavalry was chosen for the three Right Direct commands.

sentences.zh: 北面兩直，營貝、冀隸高陽關都部署。

translations.literal: The two Northern Direct commands were camped at Bei and Ji, subordinate to the Gaoyang Pass Overall Deployment.
translations.idiomatic: The two Northern Direct commands were encamped at Bei and Ji, under the Gaoyang Pass Overall Deployment.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符中，改爲貝州左直、冀州右直，後改四直。

translations.literal: In Dazhong Xiangfu, renamed Bei Prefecture Left Direct and Ji Prefecture Right Direct; later reorganized as four direct commands.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dazhong Xiangfu era they became Bei Prefecture Left Direct and Ji Prefecture Right Direct; later they were reorganized as four direct commands.

sentences.zh: 京師二，恩、冀各一。

translations.literal: Two in the capital; one each at En and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Two in the capital; one each at En and Ji.

sentences.zh: 龍衛舊號護聖。

translations.literal: Dragon Guard was formerly called Protecting Sageliness.
translations.idiomatic: Dragon Guard had formerly been Protecting Sageliness.

sentences.zh: 周廣順中，改龍捷。

translations.literal: In Zhou Guangshun, renamed Dragon Swift.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Later Zhou in Guangshun it was renamed Dragon Swift.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年，揀去衰老，以諸州所募精勁者補之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianlong, aged men were weeded out and filled with vigorous recruits from the prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianlong 2 the aged were culled and replaced with vigorous recruits drawn from the prefectures.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年，改分左、右廂。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taiping Xingguo, reorganized into left and right wings.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 2 it was divided into left and right wings.

sentences.zh: 四年，平太原，選其降兵爲揀中龍衛。

translations.literal: In year 4, when Taiyuan was pacified, surrendered troops were selected as Selected Dragon Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4, after Taiyuan fell, surrendered troops were chosen for Selected Dragon Guard.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，又揀善槍槊者爲钅屈直。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi, men skilled with spear and halberd were selected for Bent Bow Direct.

translations.idiomatic: Divine Guard: under the Jin it was called the Reverent State army; under the Zhou it was renamed Tiger Swift.

translations.idiomatic: In Jianlong 2, recruited Palace Corps from the prefectures were reviewed and used to fill vacancies.

translations.literal: In the third year of Qiande, Wang Quanbin, overall deployment of the Sichuan field headquarters, citing the merits of those who had pacified bandits under the puppet titles Persuade Transformation and Glorious Martial and other armies, requested they guard the palace guard; an edict made them all Tiger Swift.

translations.idiomatic: It was renamed in Taiping Xingguo 2.

translations.idiomatic: The old Water Tiger Wing were troops in the army trained for river combat; that year they became Divine Guard Navy, and men still fit for campaign service were also chosen from surplus members to form Selected Divine Guard.

translations.idiomatic: Tiger Wing: in the early Song it was called Bold Martial crossbowmen.

translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 2, strong brave men were chosen as Upper Iron Forest and the next rank as Lower Iron Forest.

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongxi, reorganized into left and right wings, three armies each.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi 4 it was reorganized into left and right wings, three armies each.

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, men from the army skilled in water warfare were selected as Upper Tiger Wing; also in that year Yangtze-Huai soldiers practiced in water drill were chosen at Jinming Pool, tested in battle oars, and formed as Tiger Wing.

translations.literal: Jiangsu-Zhejiang and Huainan prefectures also followed this method for selection and establishment.

translations.idiomatic: In year 7 it was renamed Tiger Wing Navy.

translations.idiomatic: Ninety in the capital and one naval command; one each at Xiangyi, Dongming, and Shan; one at Changge.

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingde, Upper Reverent Obedience was also selected and established.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingde 3 Upper Reverent Obedience was added as well.

translations.idiomatic: Martial Guard: during Taiping Xingguo, men were recruited from Hebei prefectures to form the command.

sentences.zh: 舊指揮十六，慶曆中，河北增置爲指揮六十七。

translations.idiomatic: It had formerly stood at sixteen commands; in Qingli Hebei additions brought the total to sixty-seven.

translations.idiomatic: In Chunhua 4, Wei Oar and Secure Ning troops from the Sichuan gorges escorted to the capital were also formed as Sichuan Render Loyalty.

translations.idiomatic: One command.

translations.idiomatic: In year 8, after Jiangnan was pacified, surrendered troops were added to fill it; one command.

translations.idiomatic: Selected Grateful Love: originally Shu troops; it was formed together with Grateful Favor, and the best men were also picked out as Selected Grateful Love.
